name: lookup
description:
The table with the columns of the lookup table added, row by row, by a key phrase.

A row takes the cells of the first row of the lookup table whose key is the same by the kind. A row with no match keeps empty cells; with matched_only it is dropped. The rows keep their order. A lookup column whose name the table has gets the suffix _lookup. The attribute repeated_keys of the result counts the keys that stand in the lookup table more than once. A column that is not in a table is refused, naming the columns there are.

on: the key column, or MAIN=LOOKUP when the lookup table calls it differently; without it, the first text column of each table.
kind: how two keys are the same: exact (the same text), explicit (the same in any case, with ё as е and any spaces), implicit (the same words in another order) or lemmas (the same lemmas in any order).
take: the column of the lookup table to add; repeat it for each next column; without it, every other column.
matched_only: drop the rows that have no match.

Example: semkit read phrases.csv lookup lookup/urls.csv --take url --matched-only write -
-> купить диван, /buy-divan; кресло, /kreslo

file: the lookup table; the file is read like `read` does. The key is --on, by default the working column of the table and the first text column of the lookup table.

The step adds the columns after the last column of the table; the working column stays the same. The report (stderr and --json) says how many keys repeat in the lookup table: the first row of each wins.
